hypothesis: Elementary cellular automaton rule 110, whose rule is stated in one sentence, is computationally universal (Cook 2004). The published proof is a chain of exact emulations: 2-symbol Turing machines -> 2-tag systems (Cocke/Cook, Cook 2004 section 2.1), 2-tag systems -> cyclic tag systems (Cook 2004 section 2.2), cyclic tag systems -> rule-110 glider systems (Cook 2004 sections 3-4). The first two links are fully specified constructions that can be executed and checked exactly; the third relies on the glider inventory of rule 110 (Cook 2004 figure 5), whose velocities must be present in rule-110 evolutions.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. (A) One-sentence rule: the sentence 'A cell becomes black if it or its right-hand neighbour is black, unless it and both of its neighbours are black' has at most 30 words and, evaluated as a Boolean predicate on the 8 neighbourhoods, reproduces all 8 entries of Wolfram's rule 110 (binary 01101110). (B) TM -> tag: for 30 random 2-symbol Turing machines with 2-4 states (every transition writes a bit, moves left or right, and changes to any state; no halting), each started from a random tape of 8 bits on each side of the head and run for 40 steps, Cook's 10m-symbol 2-deletion tag system (rules as printed on pp. 5-6 of Cook 2004) started from the encoded configuration reaches the encoded configuration of each successive Turing-machine step within 100000 tag steps; 100% of the 1200 step checks succeed. (C) Tag -> cyclic tag: for the same 30 tag systems plus 30 random 2-tag systems with 2-6 symbols and appendants of length 0-4, each run for 200 tag steps from a random tape (or until the tape empties), Cook's 2k-appendant cyclic tag system (symbol i -> N^(i-1) Y N^(k-i); appendants = encoded appendants then k empty ones) reproduces the encoded tag tape after every 2k cyclic-tag steps; 100% of checks. (D) Glider inventory: the velocities of all naturally occurring rule-110 gliders in Cook 2004 figure 5 (A 2/3, B -1/2, C 0, D 1/5, E and Ebar -4/15, F -1/9, G -1/3; H and the glider gun are stated by Cook not to arise naturally) are all present among the exactly periodic localized structures measured in claim-tests/wolfram-nks/wolfram2002-ch02-09/derived/measured.json (random initial conditions, 20 runs). 'Supports' requires A-D.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' if A fails (rule 110 is not the stated sentence), or if B or C fails in more than 5% of checks (the printed constructions do not emulate as claimed), or if fewer than 5 of the 7 figure-5 velocities are observed in D. Other combinations are 'mixed'. The test cannot refute Cook's theorem itself; a failure of B or C would show that the printed proof as transcribed does not work, not that no one-sentence universal system exists.
interpretation: The claim is an existence claim: at least one system with a one-sentence rule is universal. It is tested on its canonical instance, rule 110, by (A) checking that the rule really is one short sentence, (B, C) executing the first two reductions of Cook's published proof exactly on random instances, and (D) checking that the glider species the third reduction is built from exist with the stated velocities. Universality is taken in Cook's sense (emulation of a universal Turing machine on finite initial data, with the periodic background and periodic right-hand table data that Cook's construction uses; Neary and Woods 2006 later showed the emulation is polynomially efficient). The third link (cyclic tag system -> rule 110, Cook 2004 section 4) is not re-executed here: its initial conditions are long glider packets whose phases are specified only in the paper's figures.

datasets.name: Cook, M. (2004) Universality in Elementary Cellular Automata, Complex Systems 15(1):1-40
datasets.role: source of the three-link proof; sections 2.1-2.2 (pp. 4-8) give the constructions executed in B and C, figure 5 (p. 14) the glider periods used in D

datasets.name: Random 2-symbol Turing machines, their Cook tag systems and cyclic tag systems (generated by analysis.py)

generator.program_family: 2-symbol Turing machines with m in {2,3,4} states (numpy default_rng seeds 0-29); 2-deletion tag systems with 10m symbols built from them by Cook's table; cyclic tag systems with 2k appendants built by Cook's encoding; 30 additional random 2-tag systems (seeds 1000-1029, 2-6 symbols, appendant length 0-4)
generator.initial_conditions: TM: random 8 bits each side of the head, random head bit, state 0; tag/CTS: encodings of the TM configuration, or random tapes of 2-6 symbols
generator.steps: 40 TM steps per machine (<= 100000 tag steps each); 200 tag steps per 2-tag system (2k CTS steps per tag step)

datasets.role: random instances on which the emulations are checked exactly

datasets.name: Rule-110 localized periodic structures measured for claim wolfram2002-ch02-09 (this repository)
datasets.role: measured glider velocities from random initial conditions, compared with Cook 2004 figure 5
